title: Hub Product Crate Consolidation Dress Rehearsal
description: Consolidate 🌎️hub from 5 crates (semio-hub, semio-hub-directory, semio-hub-directory-{sqlite,postgres,neo4j}) down to 1 crate `semio-hub` at 🌎️hub/📦️packages/🦀️rust/, applying Shape V2 tree-purity taxonomy layout at 🌎️hub root (📇️directory/🦀️component.rs + 📇️directory/{🌐️neo4j,🐘️postgres,🪶️sqlite}/🦀️component.rs, each backend gated behind a Cargo feature). This is the first framework-family merge (product/hub role) — the dress rehearsal for the much larger os-kernel/framework wave. Backend DB driver deps (rusqlite/sqlx-postgres+sqlx-core/neo4rs) become optional+feature-gated; axum/tokio/dashmap/etc. stay unconditional. Binary target `os-hub` preserved via [[bin]] alongside [lib]. Also produce 📋️TEMPLATE-FAMILY.md (general framework/product family merge recipe) in the master ticket folder 26/08/05/CRATE-CONSOLIDATION-AND-PLUGIN-TAXONOMY-RESTRUCTURE/. Zero dependents confirmed via grep. Verify with cargo check/clippy/test (no features, all-features, each feature individually) against pre-merge test baseline, then delete old crate dirs and end with a registrar handoff block (never touching root Cargo.toml directly).
summary:
Consolidated 🌎️hub from 5 crates (semio-hub bin, semio-hub-directory, semio-hub-directory-{sqlite,postgres,neo4j}) into ONE crate `semio-hub` at 🌎️hub/📦️packages/🦀️rust/, with a Shape V2 taxonomy tree at 🌎️hub/📇️directory/{🦀️component.rs,🪶️sqlite/,🐘️postgres/,🌐️neo4j/}. First framework-family (role=hub) merge — dress rehearsal for the os-kernel/framework wave.

Test baseline (recorded before any change, via isolated per-crate `cargo test`): semio-hub-directory 0 tests; sqlite 4/4 pass; postgres 0/3 (Docker unavailable in this env — environmental, not a code bug); neo4j 0 tests (empty test mod); semio-hub bin 10 tests, 7 pass / 3 fail (pre-existing `db_document wire error: truncated at offset 2` + 2 related WS assertion failures — a real, pre-existing bug in the shared framework `db`/`store` stack, unrelated to hub, NOT fixed as part of this merge since it's out of scope and shared by many dependents). Total baseline: 17 tests, 11 pass / 6 fail.

Post-merge verification (all via isolated `--manifest-path` + temporary `[workspace]` overlay per TEMPLATE.md §3, removed before handoff): `--no-default-features` check/clippy clean, 0 tests (all green); default features (`sqlite`) check/clippy clean, 14 tests (11 pass / 3 pre-existing fail, bin tests included since gated on feature=sqlite); `--features postgres` alone check/clippy clean, 3 tests (0 pass / 3 fail — Docker unavailable, matches baseline exactly); `--features neo4j` alone check/clippy clean, 0 tests; `--all-features` check/clippy clean, 17 tests total (11 pass / 6 fail) — EXACT match to the 5-crate baseline, no duplicate test names shadowed (verified: sqlite tests under `directory::sqlite::tests::*`, postgres under `directory::postgres::tests::*`, bin under `tests::*`, all distinct).

Fixed 4 pre-existing clippy findings surfaced by full-crate `-D warnings` recompilation (map_unwrap_or x2 in bin.rs + sqlite component, needless_pass_by_value on db_error_status, another map_unwrap_or on space_kind/data_dir) and one elided-lifetime warning in the sqlite backend — all mechanical, zero behavior change.

Feature-gating design: `sqlite`/`postgres`/`neo4j` features each pull in their own optional driver dep (rusqlite / sqlx-core+sqlx-postgres / neo4rs) AND forward to `db`'s (semio-framework-os-kernel-db) own same-named feature, so directory-backend and document/blob-storage-backend selection stay in lockstep under one feature name. `sqlite` is the default feature since it's the zero-external-dependency backend the bin's own test suite already used; the bin's `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` is additionally gated on `feature = "sqlite"` so a plain `cargo test` still exercises the full binary-level WS/REST suite. Postgres's `🛢️schema.sql` (previously `include_str!`-ed) was inlined as a `const SCHEMA: &str` directly in its component.rs — Shape V2 tree purity has no home for a bare non-component data file nested in the tree, and this is a zero-behavior-change mechanical transform.

`[package.metadata.semio] role = "hub"` chosen over "framework": the taxonomy roles enum has a dedicated "hub" value for exactly this owner; "framework" is reserved for 🧰️framework's own root packages. Verified end-to-end with a scratch script calling the real `discoverPackages()` from 🟦️discovery.ts — it correctly resolves `semio-hub` with `role: "hub", id: "semio-hub", area: "legacy", maturity: "clean"` among 51 total discovered packages repo-wide. This is the first real exercise of the "hub" role value (🌎️hub's area was previously markerless/legacy with zero 📦️packages dirs).

[lib] + [[bin]] shape: old semio-hub crate had ONLY [[bin]], no library surface (zero external dependents confirmed via repo-wide grep before starting). Added [lib] anyway per the plan's instruction, since the directory trait/model/backends are now internal modules of the SAME crate that the binary itself must reach via `use semio_hub::directory::…` — this is standard Rust behavior (a [[bin]] automatically links its package's own [lib], no extra Cargo.toml entry needed) and gives future consumers a real library surface if one is ever needed.

Old crate dirs deleted (🌎️hub/⚡️implementations/, 🌎️hub/🔨️modules/) only after full verification was green. Root Cargo.toml untouched by me — see registrar handoff below. Root Cargo.toml was independently modified by a concurrent session during this ticket (unrelated churn, left as-is per instructions).

Also wrote 📋️TEMPLATE-FAMILY.md in the master ticket folder (26/08/05/CRATE-CONSOLIDATION-AND-PLUGIN-TAXONOMY-RESTRUCTURE/) — the general recipe for merging a framework/product family (not a plugin) into one Shape V2 crate: role metadata decision method, [lib]+[[bin]] handling, backend-crates-to-features recipe (incl. tying features to a sibling crate's same-named features), taxonomy tree organization without artifacts/apps vocabulary (+ the exact #[path] resolution rule for a non-inline nested mod), the non-source-asset inlining rule, the per-feature-combination verification sequence, and gotchas (concurrent-workspace churn, contended shared target/, the "which cfg arms actually read this param" trap, never-background-verification confirmed again).

    "🌎️hub/🔨️modules/📇️directory/🐘️postgres/⚡️implementations/🦀️rust",
    "🌎️hub/🔨️modules/📇️directory/🌐️neo4j/⚡️implementations/🦀️rust",

No cross-cutting files outside 🌎️hub needed edits (zero external dependents, confirmed both before and after). After the registrar adds the member line, `cargo metadata`/`cargo check --workspace` should resolve normally; I could not run a final whole-workspace check myself since the new crate isn't a member yet (by design, per the isolated-verification protocol) and root-level commands are shared/contended with other concurrent sessions.
